newsitem.title: USA: ADRs boom in first half of year: Citibank.
newsitem.headline: ADRs boom in first half of year: Citibank.

text.p: The value of American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) continued to surge in the first half of 1997, Citibank said Wednesday in a preliminary report.

Emerging market programs led the boom. While only 38 percent of the $6.2 billion raised in the the first half of 1996 was for emerging market issuers, in 1996 57 percent of the $6.4 billion raised overall was for issuers based in emerging markets.
Some of the strongest growth came from the economies of Brazil, India, Taiwan, Indonesia, Hungary, Portugal and Russia.
The average ADR share price jumped 30 percent from the first half of 1996 to the same period this year, versus a gain of 11 percent for stocks of U.S.-based issuers.

The dollar value of ADR shares traded through the end of May jumped 20 percent from the previous year, with $211.5 billion projected for the first half of 1997 against $175.9 billion in the same period the year before.
The number of shares traded in the first half of 1997 fell slightly, to 5.2 billion from 5.6 billion the year before.
Through the first half of 1997, 96 companies from 34 countries had launched new ADR programs. In the same period last year, 98 companies introduced new programs.
ADRs are U.S. securities that represent shares of a non-U.S. company and trade in the U.S. financial markets similar to the way shares of U.S. companies do.
